# Psalm 53 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For-the-choirmaster. Upon Mahalath. A-Maskil of-David.

**2** The-fool says in-his-heart, 'There-is-no God.' They-are-corrupt and-do-abominable injustice; there-is-no-one doing good.

**3** God from-heaven looks-down upon the-sons of-man, to-see if-there-is [one who] understands, [one who] seeks God.

**4** All have-turned-back; together they-are-corrupt; there-is-no-one doing good — not even one.

**5** Do-they-not know, the-workers of-iniquity, who-eat my-people [as] they-eat bread? God they-do-not call-upon.

**6** There they-feared a-fear — [where] there-was no-fear — for God scattered the-bones of-the-one-encamping-against-you; you-put-them-to-shame, for God rejected-them.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **53:1**: Nearly identical to Psalm 14, with one major difference: v.6 replaces Ps 14:5-6 with a reference to God scattering enemy bones — a more militaristic ending.

— EMET
